title: Rabbi Zekharyah ben Avkulas
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Gittin 56b relates how Jerusalem was destroyed through Bar Kamtza, who informed the government that the Jews had rebelled against them. They sent an offering through him, and he made a blemish in it. The sages wanted to offer it for the sake of peace with the government, but Rabbi Zekharyah ben Avkulas did not let them; they wanted to kill the informer, and he did not let them. Rabbi Yochanan said of this (in Tosefta Shabbat, chapter 13, the reading is “Rabbi Yose said,” which Hyman endorses as correct): “The humility of Rabbi Zekharyah ben Avkulas destroyed the Temple.” In Eichah Rabbah, on the verse “The sons of Zion,” [it relates] that Rabbi Zekharyah ben Avkulas was at the feast when Kamtza expelled Bar Kamtza, and he could have protested but did not protest.
One halakhah of his is found in Shabbat 143a: they said of him that he would turn his face behind the couch and throw them (the peels).

notes.text: Hyman’s Eichah report says Kamtza expelled Bar Kamtza; that received wording is translated, not silently replaced with the Bavli’s unnamed host. Saved Davidson Gittin56a gives the sacrifice debate; supplied56b and Hyman’s preferred Yose attribution remain visible.

The consulted Eikhah Rabbah 4 account has an unnamed host, Kamtza as his friend and Bar Kamtza as his enemy; it also names Rabbi Yose in the conclusion. Hyman’s supplied wording says Kamtza expelled Bar Kamtza and is retained as his report. The consulted Tosefta Shabbat 13 did not yield this named passage in the bounded search; the exact Tosefta edition/numbering remains unverified, not disproven.
